units.title: Postural features and assessment
units.summary: Ideal Erect Posture • Erect posture: the posture that an individual is standing at attention or told to “stand up straight” • In this posture, a plumb line falls through • Ear lob • Tip of the shoulder • Center of the hip / greater trochanter • Anterior 1/3 to middle of the knee • Just behind the ankle bone • need conscious control Understanding the Posture • Natural Spine • Cervical Lordosis • Thoracic Kyphosis • Lumbar Lordosis Effect of Pelvic Tilt on lower body posture Elbow - Carrying angle • In elbow extension & forearm supination position • Angle between the long axis of arm & the long axis of forearm • NORMAL: around 5 -15 degree Hip / Knee Q angle (Quadriceps angle • The acute angle formed by a line drawn from the ASIS to central patella and a second line drawn from central patella to tibial tubercle • Normally • Female: 15-17 degree (because of wider pelvis) • Male: 10-14 degree • A high Q angle often results in mal tracking of patella, and overtime it easily leads to anterior knee pain

units.title: Gait fundamentals
units.summary: Gait cycle The gait cycle is defined as the time interval between two successive occurrence of one of the repetitive events of walking. Stance phase & Swing phase • Swing phase • when the foot is moving forward through the air • Stance phase • Support phase, last from initial contact to toe off Gait cycle So the gait cycle can subdivide into 1. Stride length • Distance between two successive placements of the same foot. • Consists of two step lengths, left and right.

units.title: Pathological gait
units.summary: Spastic hemiplegia • the commonest neurological abnormal gait. It can occurs in cerebral palsy, cerebrovascular accident and traumatic brain injury. • A hemiplegic patient usually possesses a mixture of normal motor control, spasticity and patterned responses, he exact combination depending on the severity and location of the brain damage. Typical problems are as follows: o Foot drop on the affected side o Contracture of the calf muscles o Overactivity of both quadriceps and hamstrings o Reduced range of hip motion due to overactivity of ilipsaoas and the adductors Spastic diplegia A common manifestation of cerebral palsy.

units.title: Functional mobility tests
units.summary: Modified Functional Ambulation Categories (MFAC) Cat. Stage Definition Lyer Unable to walk / unable to sit without support>1min / assist to sit Sitter Sit without support >1min / unable to walk with 1 person assistance III Dependent Walk with 1 person assistance – level ground (continuous manual contact to support body Walker weight) Assisted Walker Walk with 1 person assistance – level ground (continuous or intermittent manual contact) Supervised Walk with standby guarding from 1 person – level ground Walker Indoor Walker Transfer, turn & walk on level ground independently, needs assistance on stairs/inclines VII Outdoor Walker Walk independently on level or non-level surfaces Timed up and Go test A score of more than or equal to fourteen seconds has been shown to indicate high risk of falls.
